articleBody:
Adding crown molding or decorative wall trim elevates a bathroom, but the high humidity and tight corners create unique hurdles. Use this preparation checklist before your installer arrives to ensure a smooth, durable installation.

- [ ] Inspect exhaust fan airflow — Confirm your bathroom fan vents completely outdoors rather than into an attic space to control moisture.
- [ ] Clear personal items and vanity counters — Remove toiletries, mirrors, and hanging towels so carpenters have unobstructed ladder access to the ceiling perimeter.
- [ ] Acclimate wood-based molding for 48 hours — Allow primed wood or MDF profiles to rest in your home environment to equalize moisture levels before cutting.
- [ ] Verify wall-to-ceiling corner angles — Check out-of-square drywall corners in advance so the installer can plan coped joints or compound miter angles.
- [ ] Confirm paint and sealant cure specifications — Review drying times on bathroom-rated caulks and adhesives to plan shower downtime accordingly.
- [ ] Inspect surrounding drywall for hidden soft spots — Address previous ceiling moisture stains or peeling paint before fastening decorative profiles over them.
- [ ] Purchase 10 to 15 percent extra trim length — Account for miter test cuts, complex corner copes, and pattern matching along long walls.
